page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor configured with 20 vCPUs and 20 physical cores at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% across stress-ng and Passmark tests. The system memory subsystem delivers strong read bandwidth of 309.72 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 135.97 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier performance in image processing, text processing, and small-model LLM inference, processing 4434.62 tokens/sec for a 135M model. Medium 7B model inference remains strong at 36.85 tokens/sec for generation, while large 70B model inference drops to average tiers.

Given the high-density memory configuration of 12.8 GB per core and the inclusion of a 48 GB NVIDIA L40S GPU, this server offers high resource density for memory-intensive and parallel computing tasks. The lack of local storage requires external storage attachments, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-to-medium LLM inference, image processing, data science pipelines, and database operations.
description: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-1xL40S is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated and memory-intensive workloads. It features a 20-core AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 256.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of VRAM. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the server delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, alongside high memory bandwidth. While it lacks local storage, it provides exceptional throughput for data processing, image manipulation, and LLM inference, particularly with small to medium models. This hardware profile makes it highly suitable for machine learning inference, database operations, and parallel computing tasks requiring substantial memory capacity per core.
